messages:
Ravi (People Ops): Quick question from a new hire: they get a monthly on-call stipend and will start unpaid parental leave mid-May. Can they keep doing 401(k) deferrals and HSA payroll contributions from that stipend while on leave?

Sam (Infra Eng): wondering if the stipend is processed as 'wages' or 'expense' matters here. we code it as a separate line item currently.

Elena (Payroll): Important: if the stipend is coded as taxable earnings (we typically use code ONCALL_STIP), it counts as eligible wages for 401(k) and for pre-tax HSA deductions in that pay period. If payroll records the period as unpaid with no wages, payroll cannot take pre-tax HSA deductions.

Elena (Payroll): Practical steps:
- Ensure the stipend is entered before payroll cutoff and marked ONCALL_STIP.
- If the employee's 401(k) election is a % or amount on file it will apply automatically to ONCALL_STIP. If they only want to defer from the stipend and not regular pay, submit a manual election change ticket.

Ravi (People Ops): What are the vendor timing and minimum amount gotchas? the hire wants $75/mo from the stipend.

Elena (Payroll): Two vendor caveats: 1) Some recordkeepers have a plan-level minimum per contribution (rare, but possible). 2) Export cadence: our 401(k) export goes out X business days after pay date; payroll changes must be in the system before cutoff (we recommend 48 hours before pay). Small amounts generally pass through fine but i will confirm with the recordkeeper for this plan.

Benefits Bot: Added link: benefits.plan.docs/401k-recordkeeper (internal access).

Sam (Infra Eng): If they make HSA contributions via payroll on the stipend, will that affect HSA employer contribution eligibility or catch-up rules?

Elena (Payroll): Employer HSA contributions follow the same payroll coding rules and will apply if payroll posts taxable wages in the period. Catch-up deferrals (age 55+) are applied per employee election; they work the same.

Ravi (People Ops): If payroll cannot do pre-tax HSA while they are unpaid, can the employee contribute directly and then claim on taxes?

Elena (Payroll): Yes: employee can make post-tax direct contributions to their HSA and claim the deduction on Form 8889. We'll add KB instructions for both workflows and the payroll cutoff timeline.

Ravi (People Ops): Great. Please ping the recordkeeper about the $75 acceptance and min rules and then I'll update the benefits KB.

Elena (Payroll): Will ping recordkeeper and draft KB blurb: "Deferring stipends and leave interactions" including timelines, payroll code (ONCALL_STIP), and manual ticket instructions. Tagging @Ravi for review when draft is ready.

Ravi (People Ops): Thanks all :raised_hands:

(End of thread)
